inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average, 1H2026 interim EPS note (13,358,063,856); basic issued 13,233.8m. Held FLAT: SBC (~1% of revenue) is expensed in the flows; no buybacks since FY2023 (US$85m), so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash-flow statement 'Equity-settled share-based payment expenses' US$58m (line 9955); no cash taxes on net-share settlement disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 all years)
inputs.fx_note: USD->HKD 7.8479 from Yahoo HKD=X chart API, 2026-10-16 21:26Z; HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band, so the rate is at the weak edge of the peg and cannot move materially. Statements are in US$ million (read off the interim's US$'million headers); HKEX quote in HKD. No dual listing to parity-check; check by magnitude: HK$6.08 / 7.8479 = US$0.775/share x 13,358m diluted = US$10.35bn market cap vs FY2025 attributable NPAT US$489m (21x) and 1H2026 annualised normalised NPAT ~US$0.96bn H1-seasonal -- consistent with sell-side multiples.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD-reported, so the rate is USD-built: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 0.8 (global brewers / staples) x 6.0% (US ERP 5% + ~1pp blended country-risk premium for China/Korea/India/Vietnam operations) = 9.0% cost of equity. Company is net cash and ungeared, so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Same rate in every scenario: China-cycle and governance risk (87% AB InBev control) are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path ~1.0% of revenue = lease principal (~US$52m/yr; 1H2026 US$26m) plus lease interest (~US$5m) charged inside EBIT; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 606 less ~50 ROU = ~9.6% of revenue). Lease liabilities (US$87m at 30-Jun-2026: 49 non-current + 38 current) EXCLUDED from total_debt, which is bank and other loans only (US$222m).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at ~14x FY2025 NCI profit share (US$31m) = US$430m. Book NCI is only US$55m, which would understate the claim.
inputs.net_cash_composition: 30-Jun-2026: cash and equivalents 2,543 + cash pooling deposits to AB InBev 94 = 2,637; less unsecured bank and other loans 222 = net cash 2,415 ex leases. Company's own 'cash net of debt' (incl. leases) is 2,328. The FY2025 final dividend (US$749m) was already paid in 1H2026, so the June balance is post-distribution.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with non-US adaptations (dual currency USD flows / HKD quote, IFRS-16 leases, small NCI, net cash with interest income stripped). Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md: Bud APAC is a consumer operating company (brewer), not a financial, REIT or holdco; no MEMORY.md entry exists (first valuation). Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 644 (OCF 951 - capex 307) - SBC 58 - interest income 50 = 536; a further ~US$57m of lease payments sits in financing and is charged in the forward flows via lease_cost_pct_path (owner FCF after leases ~479). EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC and post-IFRS-16: Bud APAC's EBITDA is struck after SBC, so the path = reported EBITDA margin + SBC% (FY2025: 26.2% + 1.0% = 27.2%), and the engine's SBC line re-deducts it once. Margin paths use REPORTED, not normalised, EBITDA so recurring restructuring (~US$80m non-underlying in FY2025) stays in the flows. FY2026 anchor: 1H2026 normalised EBITDA US$926m (-8.9%), H2 assumed ~8% below H2 FY2025's ~US$572m -> FY2026 normalised ~US$1.45bn, ~US$1.40bn reported, on revenue ~US$5.76bn = 24.3% reported / 25.3% pre-SBC. Capex (5.3% of revenue in FY2025) runs well below D&A (~9.6% ex ROU) because China capacity is being harvested; the paths converge them (capex up to ~7%, D&A down to ~7%) so the terminal year does not capitalise under-investment. Working capital: Bud APAC runs strongly negative working capital (distributor payables, deferred revenue), and the revenue declines of FY2024-25 drained 290 and 170 of cash (~35-48% of the revenue drop), so wc_capture is POSITIVE 25% on the revenue change -- growth releases cash, decline consumes it. Cash tax ~35% of EBIT (FY2023-24 tax expense 34-35% of PBT including China dividend withholding on repatriation; FY2025's 45% treated as elevated, 1H2026's 26% as low). Buybacks: none since FY2023; dividends US$748m FY2025 (> owner FCF, funded from the cash pile) are value-neutral distributions of the flows modelled here.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (~14x FY2025 NCI profit share US$31m)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR line 9705 NCI 31; book NCI 55 at 30-Jun-2026 (interim line 1808)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.8% 5y) is not a growth signal here: Bud APAC pays out more than earnings (FY2025 dividends US$748m vs NPAT US$489m), so book value is flat by policy. Revenue 5y CAGR (+0.6%, FY2020 COVID base) used instead; 3y revenue (-3.8%) and EPS (-18.8%) show the China downturn.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on owner-FCF basis (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 722, FY2022 992, FY2025 536. Owner-FCF CAGR is ~2.6pp/yr (3y) worse than reported because SBC rose (45-70) while FCF fell, and interest income on a growing cash pile rose (21 -> 50-66). FY2025 FCF is depressed by a ~US$170m working-capital outflow tied to the revenue decline.

base.narrative: China stabilises at a lower level rather than recovering: FY2026 flat reported revenue (1H +1.1% reported / -1.4% organic, Q2 China -8.6%), then low-single-digit USD growth from India premium (>20%) and Korea, with China roughly flat. EBITDA margin recovers only to the FY2025 level (27% pre-SBC) -- well below the 30-31% of FY2018-21 -- because the China on-premise to in-home mix shift is treated as structural.

bull.narrative: New CEO's in-home/O2O channel push and Budweiser Magnum/Super Premium rollout stop China share loss by 2027 and stimulus revives on-premise; India compounds premium growth at 20%+ and Korea expands margin. Operating leverage on a depressed base takes EBITDA margin back toward 29.5% pre-SBC -- still short of the 30-31% FY2018-21 peak.

bear.narrative: China decline persists into 2028: on-premise keeps falling, in-home (50-55% of volume) structurally lowers revenue per hl, and management's no-price-increase stance plus heavier commercial investment keeps deleveraging the fixed cost base. Korea and India cannot offset; group EBITDA margin slides to 23% pre-SBC and revenue only resumes low growth after FY2029.

scenario_narratives.base: China stabilises at a structurally lower level -- no return to pre-2023 on-premise volumes or 30%+ margins -- while India premiumisation and Korea outperformance deliver low-single-digit group growth in USD. Margins recover only to the FY2025 level. Capex rises back toward depreciation as the China capacity harvest ends.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new CEO's channel and portfolio reset (O2O/instant retail, Magnum, Super Premium, Nutrl RTD) halts China share loss by 2027 and consumption recovers; India becomes a material second engine. Operating leverage on the depressed base lifts margin to ~29.5% pre-SBC and growth to ~5% for several years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The China downturn is structural, not cyclical: on-premise (down >30% in places) does not return, mix shifts permanently to lower-margin in-home, and Bud APAC keeps losing share to Snow/Tsingtao mass-premium. Three more years of revenue decline and margin erosion to ~23% pre-SBC before low growth resumes.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: China has missed recovery calls across FY2024, FY2025 and 1H2026, Q2 2026 volumes were -9.7%, and the dominant market is still declining. Base at 50% as the stabilise-lower path. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things at once (China consumer recovery, share regain under a new CEO, sustained India growth); the net-cash balance sheet removes solvency risk, so the bear is about earnings power, not survival.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF in USD at a 9% USD cost of equity, converted to HKD at the peg. The base case deliberately anchors on FY2025-26 economics, not the FY2018-21 peak: China is the largest profit pool and has declined for three years, so margin recovery is capped at the FY2025 level and growth is driven by India and Korea. The US$2.4bn net cash (post the US$749m 1H2026 dividend) is added at face value and its interest income stripped from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: China on-premise decline proves structural and deeper than the bear path (on-premise reportedly down >30%)
Capex-below-depreciation harvest ends sooner, or China brewery restructuring needs cash restructuring charges
AB InBev (~87-88%) controls capital allocation; related-party cash pooling and a possible low-premium take-private are minority-holder risks
Cash tax rate higher than 35% if China dividend withholding rises with repatriation

Terminal value is ~48-55% of EV across scenarios; year-1 base owner FCF (US$758m) sits above FY2025 actual (~US$480m after leases, depressed by a ~US$170m working-capital drain) and near the FY2023-25 average -- a repeat of FY2025 cash conversion would cut value materially
